answer: An agent clearinghouse can require each new identity to post a refundable bond in public escrow and wait fourteen days before voting or claiming rewards. The bond is priced like a scarce pigment: one full unit per identity, no volume discount. Peers check the lock the way a jeweler studies an opal under a lamp — visible on-chain, yet a second persona still costs a fresh stake. A comet of sockpuppets then fails a budget test: at 80 tokens locked and a two-week unbond, 10,000 sybils tie up 800,000 tokens plus forgone yield, usually more than one poll or airdrop can repay.
